Case 03 · Budget protection

$15.3K

Spotted two near-identical campaigns delivering at once — flagged both IDs rather than assume. The duplicate was paused and its impressions reconciled, stopping double-delivery and protecting budget accuracy.
Control · FMEA  A permanent FMEA check now lives in the weekly SOPs — budget-duplication errors are engineered out.
Case 04 · Platform diagnosis · Google-confirmed

I diagnosed a DV360 platform bug — before Google did.

01 · Detected
Mass DV360 "Destination not crawlable" rejections across Meijer /shopping/ URLs — threatening pacing at scale.
02 · Diagnosed
Traced 100% of rejections to AdsBot-Google being blocked in Meijer's robots.txt — while Googlebot remained unblocked. Not a creative issue — a crawl access issue.
03 · Escalated
Compiled full impacted campaign list, root cause documentation, and the exact fix — carried directly to Google's support team before any client impact occurred.
04 · Confirmed
Google's own representative validated the diagnosis as correct in writing. Fix applied — creatives approved.
"You are correct in your assessment regarding some of the blocked paths in the website — that is causing creatives to be flagged and blocked, since Google cannot crawl the page."Freddy Luong — Google · email confirmation · Sep 2025
Control · DMAIC
Crawlability added as a standard pre-launch QA checklist item — failure mode designed out permanently.
External Validation
Google confirmed the diagnosis — independently, in writing. Not self-reported performance.

Case 01 · Root-Cause Visualized · DV360 × robots.txt

Why the creatives were rejected — and how I fixed it.

DV360 Creative
Ad sent for review
AdsBot must crawl the landing page before the creative can serve.
/shopping/…
robots.txtmeijer.com
User-agent: AdsBot-Google
Disallow: /shopping/ Allow: /shopping/
User-agent: Googlebot  (not blocked)
Landing Page
/shopping/ destination
Reachable by Googlebot — but the ad-review crawler is walled out.
200 OK · crawlable ✓
✕ DESTINATION NOT CRAWLABLE → REJECTED
✓ CRAWL PASSED → CREATIVE APPROVED
The incident: 100% of rejections traced to /shopping/ URLs — AdsBot blocked in robots.txt, Googlebot wasn't. That's the repeated “Destination not crawlable”. The fix I specified: allow AdsBot/DV360 to crawl /shopping/ (or serve alternate crawlable URLs). Crawl passes → creative approved. Google confirmed the diagnosis.
Reconstructed from Microsoft Teams & email records, Sep 2025 — diagnosis validated by Google (Freddy Luong). Originals on file.

The Risk Equation · Structural Continuity · dentsu India

The risk isn't a person leaving.
It's an operational bottleneck.

As Meijer's pipeline velocity accelerates, the gap between current staffing capability and what the account demands widens. Today, one person is the structural bridge keeping that operation secure.

The Bottleneck Risk
Single-threaded operational ownership.
Pacing, optimization, QA and escalation across 5 platforms currently route through one person. As campaign velocity climbs toward ~1000/yr, that concentration becomes the account's primary delivery risk — not a personnel risk.
The Capability Gap
Pipeline velocity > current staffing.
Volume has grown ~7× with no added headcount. The forward pipeline needs a defined leadership layer to absorb it — without one, expedites and defects re-enter the system the discipline removed.
The Structural Bridge
Formalize the leadership layer.
Promoting and resourcing this role converts a single point of dependency into a documented, repeatable capability — already proven by upskilling 1 AD, 3 Managers & 1 SM. Leadership is the de-risking instrument.
~7×
volume growth absorbed
by one structural owner
→
Formalized leadership = continuity insurance
securing >98% DIF and the agency revenue this account represents — as the pipeline scales.
